text:
Talia Benson: Hey all — quick cross-team ask for the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint.

We need to lock the “top hosted models” list + the traffic mix assumptions (prompt len + gen len + prefill/decode ratio + tool/JSON %). This becomes the official benchmark suite scope, so I want sign-off on representativeness.

Can PM/Applied ML confirm:
1) Which 5–8 models count as “top hosted” for last 30d (tokens), excluding preview/legacy?
2) Any must-include workloads (tool-calling, structured output, long-context)?
3) Who’s the sign-off chain so we don’t bikeshed later?

Henry Cho: Pulling usage now. Do we mean “hosted API chat/generate” only (exclude embeddings/rerank)?

Talia Benson: Yes — chat/generate. We can do embeddings separately later; kernel sprint scope is attention/matmul heavy.

Aditya Rao: +1 on excluding embeddings for this sprint. For Optimize we still care about tool-calling + JSON mode though (customers ask about it constantly).

Henry Cho: Ok. From Looker “hosted_tokens_30d” (prod, excluding internal eval traffic), top 6 are pretty stable. Proposed list (model ids as in catalog):
- `rw/llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- `rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct`
- `rw/mixtral-8x7b-instruct`
- `rw/qwen2.5-72b-instruct`
- `rw/gemma-2-27b-instruct`
- `rw/mistral-7b-instruct`

These cover ~82–85% of chat/generate tokens depending on week. The next 10 are long tail / region-specific.

(reaction: :thumbsup: from Aditya Rao)

Jonas Weber: From Applied ML side, those 6 make sense. Only nuance: we should include at least one “long-context heavy” case because FP8 quality regressions tend to show up there + decode gets more sensitive.

Do we have a “32k context enabled” variant for any of these in hosted? (llama 70b + qwen 72b are usually where we see it)

Rina Kobayashi: We can include long-context as a workload slice rather than a separate model. Harness can sweep prompt len distributions (e.g., 512/2k/8k/16k) and keep model fixed.

Claire Dubois: Agree on list. For representativeness sign-off, we should explicitly document:
- time window + metric (tokens vs requests)
- inclusion/exclusion (preview models, internal canary traffic, dedicated pools)
- traffic stratification (region, tier)

Otherwise we’ll get “but my customer uses X” feedback.

Also: please define “top” as % coverage threshold (e.g., >=80% of hosted tokens) rather than “top N” so we can defend it.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel team is fine with 6 for the full matrix. If we can only run 4 on L4 due to time, my preference is 70B + 8B + Mixtral + Qwen (covers big + small + MoE).

Sofia Ivanova: For scheduler work, we need the prefill/decode mix + concurrency assumptions. “Pure prefill microbench” is not enough — end-to-end wins flip when you interleave decode.

Henry Cho: On mix assumptions, I can share rough aggregates:
- Median prompt ~650–900 tokens (varies by model), p95 ~3.5k
- Median gen ~220–320 tokens, p95 ~900
- Tool/JSON mode ~6–9% of requests (but skewed to a few customers)

Not sure on prefill/decode ratio; can derive from TTFT/TPOT telemetry if we want.

Talia Benson: This is great. Proposal:
- Model list = Henry’s top 6 (above). Coverage goal >=80% hosted chat/generate tokens (30d).
- Workload slices in suite v3:
  (a) default mix (prompt median/p95 as above)
  (b) long-context slice (8k/16k prompts) on 70B + Qwen
  (c) structured output/tool-calling slice (~10% weight) on 8B + 70B
  (d) mixed prefill/decode concurrency slice (Sofia + Rina to define)

Sign-off:
- PM/Perf transparency: Henry (with Aditya consulted)
- Applied ML representativeness + quality guardrails: Jonas (Claire consulted for methodology rigor)
- Final “benchmark suite v3” doc owner: Rina

Any objections by EOD tomorrow? If none, I’ll treat this as locked for the sprint plan.

Claire Dubois: No objections. Please add a short note that claims/results are for “hosted API configuration, pinned runtime + driver/CUDA”, etc. (variance + reproducibility footnotes).

Jonas Weber: +1, and please flag that any default FP8 enablement still requires eval sign-off per model (esp long-context slice). But list itself is good.

Aditya Rao: Works for me. If we end up publishing anything externally later, we’ll need the exact footnotes + the “coverage” statement. But for internal decisioning, this is perfect.

Henry Cho: Confirmed on my end. I’ll drop the Looker link + snapshot numbers in the sprint plan doc so we have an audit trail.

Talia Benson: Awesome — thanks all. I’ll update the sprint plan + methodology page with:
- top 6 list
- coverage definition
- workload slices + sign-off owners

(reaction: :white_check_mark: from Talia Benson)
